bug_semantics: Apache MINA ObjectSerializationDecoder / IoBuffer.getObject() deserializes untrusted Java streams through a custom ObjectInputStream that consults an acceptMatchers allow-list in resolveClass (and later in readClassDescriptor) but does not override resolveProxyClass. A payload containing TC_PROXYCLASSDESC makes JDK ObjectInputStream.readProxyDesc() call the default resolveProxyClass(interfaces), which Class.forName()s each interface via latestUserDefinedLoader() and constructs java.lang.reflect.Proxy without checking acceptMatchers, bypassing the allow-list (ZDRES-232, CWE-502). Separately, the type-1 readClassDescriptor path called Class.forName(className, true, classLoader) after the allow-list check, so an allow-listed class name still ran <clinit> during descriptor resolution before any instance was built (ZDRES-233).
flaw_origin: The incomplete allow-list was first written on 2.2.X in 691a9df5a0aff0dddeedc5181f6e5832ee90dcea (2024-11-04, subject 'pom.xml') by emmanuel lecharny. That commit added acceptMatchers plus IoBuffer.accept() and filtered only the clazz != null branch of resolveClass; it did not override resolveProxyClass. Parent 23e6ee17bae46bb8e7a76dd7aeb508ec89e76a25 already had the custom ObjectInputStream and Class.forName(className, true, classLoader) in readClassDescriptor (originally DIRMINA-481 / 2f8af59602e5ca5185c7f580b9ddff28a89de247, 2007) but no allow-list. Parallel first-writes of the same incomplete control landed on 2.1.X (cdb59eb6131696a440870ab89ad0e20804eb5ca7) and 2.0.X (834396355766e0c8f6bbf0493d4588b3fa9d347d) on 2024-11-06. Later incomplete-fix cca24d646c898adf7e01a765ebf6d677cc02b696 (2.2.7) moved the allow-list check before Class.forName in readClassDescriptor and always-filtered resolveClass, but kept initialize=true despite a comment saying initialize=false and still omitted resolveProxyClass.
